finding: CMS_COLLECTION_BOUND and CMS_COLLECTION_UNBOUND are not just listener-less — they have no PRODUCER either: bindCollection()/unbindCollection() are called by nothing outside their own unit test, so the repeater (list-of-records) feature has no door anywhere in the editor.
evidence: CMSBindingManager.ts:223 `this.composer.emit(EVENTS.CMS_COLLECTION_BOUND, {elementId, collectionId})` and :233 the UNBOUND twin; grep of both constants across src/ returns only events.ts:621,623, those two emit lines and CMSBindingManager.test.ts:293,324. Repo-wide grep for `bindCollection(` on the CMS manager returns CMSBindingManager.ts:208 (definition) and __tests__/CMSBindingManager.test.ts:281,301,317,335,345,363 only — engine/data/DataManager.ts:394 is a DIFFERENT bindCollection (generic data, not CMS).
fix: Either build the entry point (a Repeater toggle in the inspector that calls composer.cms.bindings.bindCollection with the picked collection) or delete bindCollection/unbindCollection, the two events, CMSCollectionBinding, exportCollectionBindings/importCollectionBindings and RepeaterRenderer together.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollectionBinding -> bind a repeater to a collection -> CMS_COLLECTION_BOUND -> Canvas/Inspector/Export -> nothing: no UI can create the binding, so no element ever repeats

finding: RepeaterRenderer — 288 lines that expand one clone per record, with nested-repeater recursion and HTML escaping — is instantiated nowhere in the product; only its own test file constructs it, so a collection's records can never be rendered as a list on any page or in any export.
evidence: grep `new RepeaterRenderer` across src/ hits only engine/cms/__tests__/RepeaterRenderer.test.ts (:70,76,85,98,132,155,174,195,212,231,248,263,284,299,315,330,348,375,391,410,436,467,504,545,574,584). engine/cms/index.ts:9 exports it; Composer.ts:271-275 builds only `{collections, bindings}` under `this.cms` — there is no `cms.repeaters`. ExportEngine.ts never imports it (only CMSExportResolver, :18).
fix: Wire expandRepeaters() into ExportEngine.exportAllPages and into the canvas content path (beside useCMSPreview) once MOD-A-01's entry point exists — or delete the file with the binding API.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem[] -> expand a repeater -> (never invoked) -> Canvas + ExportEngine -> a bound list renders as a single static template element on canvas and in the published page

finding: Element→field bindings live only in a JS Map and are in NO persistence path: ProjectData has no bindings field, and BaseBindingManager.export()/import() are never called for the CMS manager — so every binding is lost on reload, and a publish after a reload ships the placeholder text the CMS was supposed to replace.
evidence: BaseBindingManager.ts:72 `private bindings: Map<string, T[]>`; :147 export() and :160 import() exist — grep for `bindings.export(`/`bindings.import(` across src/ returns nothing outside __tests__. shared/types/project.ts:30-49 ProjectData = {version, pages, pagesOrder, styles, assets, metadata, settings, dsSchemaVersion} — no bindings field. Composer.ts:603-615 exportProject() returns exactly those keys. CMSBindingManager.ts:68 collectionBindings is a second unpersisted Map with the same problem.
fix: Add `cmsBindings?: {fields: Record<string, CMSElementBinding[]>; collections: Record<string, CMSCollectionBinding>}` to ProjectData, write it in exportProject() from bindings.export()+exportCollectionBindings(), and restore it in importProject() — after PROJECT_LOADED so element ids exist.
chain: CMS -> CMSElementBinding -> bind a text element to a field -> (no snapshot write) -> Save/Load/Publish -> reload the editor and every binding is gone; the next publish deploys the pre-binding placeholder copy with no warning

finding: Publishing or unpublishing a record refreshes nothing on the canvas: both binding re-apply and the canvas preview subscribe to content:created/updated/deleted only, and CollectionManager emits content:published INSTEAD OF content:updated on that transition — so the one save that matters most leaves the canvas showing the stale value.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:317-323 — `if (updates.status === 'published' && existing.status !== 'published') emit(CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED) else if (...) emit(CMS_CONTENT_UNPUBLISHED) else emit(CMS_CONTENT_UPDATED)` (mutually exclusive). CMSBindingManager.ts:75-77 subscribes to 'content:created','content:updated','content:deleted' only. useCMSPreview.ts:123-124 subscribes to 'content:updated','content:created' only. useContentPanel.ts:162 saves data+status in one updateContentItem call, so editing a draft and ticking Published emits only CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED.
fix: Add EVENTS.CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED and CMS_CONTENT_UNPUBLISHED to both subscription lists (CMSBindingManager.ts:75-77 and useCMSPreview.ts:123-128); useCmsSync.ts:96-97 already subscribes to both and is the model.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem -> publish a record -> CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED -> Canvas (useCMSPreview) + CMSBindingManager.reapplyAll -> neither listens; the canvas keeps the draft value until an unrelated edit or a reload

finding: Deleting a collection leaves every element bound to it silently broken: CMSBindingManager subscribes to no collection-level event, so the bindings stay in the map, resolve to an empty string, and the export skips empty values — the published page keeps whatever placeholder text was in the tree.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:162 emits CMS_COLLECTION_DELETED; its only listeners are ContentTab.tsx:97 (reload the panel) and useCmsSync.ts:93 (mirror the delete to the server). CMSBindingManager.ts:75-77 subscribes to content:* only. CMSBindingManager.ts:120-128 — queryContent on a missing collection returns [] so `items.find` is undefined and resolveBinding returns `fallback || ''`. CMSExportResolver.ts:85 `if (!value) return;` — an empty resolution is skipped, leaving the original markup.
fix: Subscribe CMSBindingManager to CMS_COLLECTION_DELETED and CMS_COLLECTION_UPDATED: drop bindings whose collectionId is gone (emitting BINDING_REMOVED so the inspector banner updates) and reapplyAll on a field-schema change. Warn before the delete when getAllCollectionBindings()/getBindings() reference it.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection -> delete a collection -> CMS_COLLECTION_DELETED -> CMSBindingManager + Inspector BindingBanner -> no listener: the inspector still shows 'bound to <deleted collection>' and the page publishes stale placeholder copy

finding: Deleting or renaming a FIELD breaks every element bound to it with no signal — the fields screen does not check bindings and CMSBindingManager never re-applies on a schema change, so the binding silently degrades to its fallback.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:221-230 deleteField -> updateCollection -> emit CMS_COLLECTION_UPDATED (:149). Listeners: ContentTab.tsx:96 (panel reload) and useCmsSync.ts:92 (server mirror) only. CMSBindingManager holds `fieldSlug` (CMSBindingManager.ts:39) and resolves `item.data[fieldSlug]` (:131) — an absent slug returns `fallback || ''`. useContentPanel.ts:202-209 deleteField calls straight through with no binding check; ContentViews FieldsView offers no usage count.
fix: On CMS_COLLECTION_UPDATED, reapplyAll() and drop bindings whose fieldSlug no longer exists in the collection; block/confirm deleteField when any element binds that slug, with the count.
chain: CMS -> CMSField -> delete a field -> CMS_COLLECTION_UPDATED -> CMSBindingManager + Content/Fields screen -> no listener and no reverse index: bound elements fall back to empty and nobody is told

finding: A CMS-only change never registers as an edit to the site, so the editor tells the user there is nothing to publish while the live site's dynamic pages are stale: CollectionManager holds no composer reference and never marks the project dirty, and the server's CMS writes never touch site.lastEditedAt — the exact field the unpublished-changes flag is computed from.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:35 `export class CollectionManager extends EventEmitter` — no composer parameter anywhere in the file, no markDirty call (contrast CMSBindingManager.ts:222 which does call composer.markDirty()). server/services/cms.service.ts:82-99 upsertEntry and :33-58 upsertCollection write cms_entries/cms_collections only — no site update. PublishService.ts:174 `hasUnpublishedChanges: publishedAt && editedAt ? editedAt.getTime() > publishedAt.getTime() : null` reading site.lastEditedAt.
fix: Stamp `site.lastEditedAt = new Date()` inside upsertEntry/upsertCollection/deleteEntry/deleteCollection in cms.service.ts (sites.service.ts:196,225,315 is the existing pattern).
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem -> edit and publish a record -> (no dirty flag, no lastEditedAt bump) -> Topbar/Publish -> the site reads 'no unpublished changes' and the visitor keeps seeing the old record

finding: The same missing lastEditedAt stamp makes a client approval un-stale-able by content: a client signs off, someone rewrites every record, and the approval still reads as current because staleness compares site.lastEditedAt to the approval time and CMS writes never move it.
evidence: server/services/client-review.service.ts:171-172 `review.site.lastEditedAt !== null && review.site.lastEditedAt.getTime() > review.resolvedAt.getTime()`; server/services/review.service.ts:210,241 reads the same field. cms.service.ts upsertEntry (:82-99) / upsertCollection (:33-58) never write it.
fix: Same one-line fix as MOD-A-07 — the stamp makes both the publish flag and the approval-staleness check honest at once.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem -> edit a record after sign-off -> (no lastEditedAt bump) -> Review / client sign-off -> the approval is reported fresh over content the client never saw

finding: The 'Collection -> Dynamic Page' link does not exist in the editor at all: nothing in packages/editor calls cms.dynamicPages or cms.generateDynamicPages, and the Pages panel has zero references to CMS — so a page-generating collection is invisible in the one place the user goes to look at their pages.
evidence: Repo-wide grep for `dynamicPages`/`generateDynamicPages` outside tests hits only server/trpc/routers/cms.ts:81,92 and server/services/cms.service.ts:152,187 — no editor call site. `grep -ri 'cms\|collection' packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/pages/` returns nothing. The only in-editor surface that mentions generated pages is DynamicPagesView (ContentViews.tsx:600), buried three levels into the Content drawer.
fix: Either call cms.dynamicPages from the Pages panel and list the generated routes as read-only children of their template page, or drop the query procedure — as it stands it is an orphan procedure (the shape memory `feedback_orphan_procedure_is_a_missing_door` names).
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection.pageSlugPattern -> set a URL pattern -> (no event, no query) -> Pages panel -> the pages a collection will generate appear in no page list, no page tree and no preview until they show up on the live site

finding: A dynamic-page collection contributes ZERO pages at publish unless pageTemplatePath matches an export filename exactly, and the only field that sets it is free text in the create wizard whose placeholder shows a path format the exporter can never produce.
evidence: server/services/cms.service.ts:234 `where: {siteId, pageSlugPattern: {not: null}, pageTemplatePath: {not: null}}` then :240 `pages.find(p => p.path === col.pageTemplatePath)` with `if (!template) continue`. Publish page paths come from ExportEngine.ts:716 `this.pageHrefs.get(page.id) ?? 'index.html'`, built at :788-797 as flat `index.html` / `<slug>.html`. CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:441 placeholder is 'Template page path — blog/_template/index.html' — a nested path buildPageHrefs never emits. ContentTab.tsx:311-313 (the only edit path) saves pageSlugPattern alone. Screen half already filed as W-C-22.
fix: Replace the free-text field with a Select over composer.elements.getAllPages(), storing the value buildPageHrefs will produce for that page, and expose the same picker in DynamicPagesView.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection.pageTemplatePath -> type a template path -> appendDynamicPagesToPublish -> Publish -> the find() misses, the loop continues, and the publish silently deploys zero of the promised pages

finding: Nothing at publish time tells the user their dynamic pages will not ship: runPrePublishChecks has six checks and not one of them is about CMS, so the only warning about an unbound template or an unpublished record set is buried in a Content sub-screen the publisher may never open.
evidence: server/services/publish.service.ts:50-105 — the complete checks list is Vercel connection, Pages ready, SEO configured, Domain connected, Empty pages, Favicon. `grep -i 'cms\|collection' server/services/publish.service.ts` returns only the appendDynamicPagesToPublish import (:5) and its call (:329). resolveDynamicPages (cms.service.ts:152) already computes exactly the number a check would need and is called by nothing.
fix: Add a 'Dynamic pages' check: for each collection with a pageSlugPattern, fail/warn when pageTemplatePath is null or matches no page path, and warn when the published-entry count is 0. resolveDynamicPages already returns the row shape.
chain: CMS -> dynamic pages -> click Publish -> runPrePublishChecks -> Publish panel -> the checklist passes green over a collection that will emit nothing

finding: Generated dynamic pages are invisible to search: they are appended server-side after the export, so they can never reach the editor's sitemap — and a publish emits no sitemap at all, because exportPublishPages calls exportAllPages without includeSitemap or baseUrl.
evidence: editor/shell/exportPublishPages.ts:39 `exportAllPages({ format: 'html', minify: true })`; ExportEngine.ts:726 `if (options.includeSitemap && options.baseUrl)` — both undefined, so no sitemap.xml is produced. Even when produced, SitemapGenerator.generate(pages, this.pageHrefs) (:727-729) sees only editor pages, while dynamic pages are added later at server/services/publish.service.ts:329 -> cms.service.ts:229-247.
fix: Generate the sitemap in appendDynamicPagesToPublish's caller — after the page-set is final — so both static and generated routes are in it, and pass baseUrl from the site's domain.
chain: CMS -> generated pages -> publish -> appendDynamicPagesToPublish -> SEO / sitemap.xml -> the routes exist on the deployment but appear in no sitemap, and the deployment has no sitemap to appear in

finding: A dynamic page's SEO comes only from two patterns that can be set once, at collection-creation, and the injection is naive: the generated <title> is APPENDED to a head that already carries the template page's own <title>, so every generated page ships two title tags and no canonical, OG or twitter tags.
evidence: cms.service.ts:206-213 — seoTags = `<title>...</title>` + optional meta description, then `html.includes('</head>') ? html.replace('</head>', seoTags+'</head>')`. The template's head is produced by ExportEngine.exportPageToHtml (:805-813) which already writes the page's SEO. pageSeoTitle/pageSeoDescription are written only at CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:212-213; DynamicPagesView saves pageSlugPattern only (ContentTab.tsx:311-313); `grep -i 'collection|cms|dynamic' SeoScreen.tsx` returns nothing.
fix: Replace the existing <title> rather than appending, extend the injection to description/canonical/og:title/og:description, and surface the two pattern fields in DynamicPagesView beside the slug pattern (and in the SEO screen).
chain: CMS -> pageSeoTitle/pageSeoDescription -> publish -> generateDynamicPages -> SEO -> two <title> tags per generated page, no canonical/OG, and no way to edit the patterns after creation

finding: A binding to any record outside the 50 most recently updated resolves to nothing: resolveBinding queries the collection with no limit and queryContent silently defaults to 50, then searches only that page for the bound record id.
evidence: CMSBindingManager.ts:120-126 `const items = await this.cmsManager.queryContent({collectionId, filter: {}}); const item = items.items.find(i => i.id === itemId); if (!item) return fallback || '';`. CollectionManager.ts:383 `const limit = options.limit || 50;` and :386 `items: items.slice(offset, offset+limit)`; CollectionStorage.ts:185 sorts by updatedAt desc, so the window is the 50 most recently touched records.
fix: Use Storage.loadContentItem(itemId) (CollectionStorage.ts:191) or getContentItem(id) for a single-record binding — the paged query is the wrong instrument for an id lookup.
chain: CMS -> CMSElementBinding.itemId -> bind to an older record -> resolveBinding -> Canvas + Export -> the element shows its fallback (usually empty), and the export skips it, so the placeholder ships

finding: A DRAFT record's values are published to the live site: resolveBinding never filters on status, and static resolution is the publish default — so an element bound to an unfinished record deploys that record's text.
evidence: CMSBindingManager.ts:110-139 resolveBinding — no status filter anywhere; queryContent is called with `{collectionId, filter: {}}` and CollectionManager.ts:355-358 applies a status filter only when options.status is set. ExportEngine.ts:700-702 `mode: options.cmsMode ?? 'static'` and exportPublishPages.ts:39 passes no cmsMode, so publish always resolves. Contrast the dynamic-page path, which filters `status: 'PUBLISHED'` (cms.service.ts:200).
fix: Resolve a published export against published records only (or fall back and flag the element in the pre-publish checks), matching generateDynamicPages' rule.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem(status=draft) -> publish the site -> CMSExportResolver.resolveStatic -> Published site -> unfinished draft copy is live, with no warning at publish time

finding: Server hydration is additive by collection id and never updates, so cross-device CMS edits only ever reach a device that has never seen the collection: rename a collection, add a field or edit a record on machine A and machine B keeps the old copy forever.
evidence: services/cmsSync.ts:124-126 `const localIds = new Set((await Storage.loadCollections()).map(c => c.id)); for (const rc of remote) { if (localIds.has(rc.id)) continue; ...}` — the entries fetch at :145-154 lives INSIDE that skipped branch, so an existing collection's entries are never re-read either. Header comment at :62-65 states the intent ('only collections whose id isn't already local are written, so a local unsynced edit is never clobbered').
fix: Reconcile by updatedAt instead of by presence: pull the remote row when remote.updatedAt > local.updatedAt and no local write for that id is pending in the SyncRetryQueue, and always re-list entries for every collection.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection/CMSContentItem -> edit on device A -> cms.entries.upsert (server) -> device B's hydrate -> the id is already local so the row is skipped: device B shows stale content for the life of the store

finding: Content entries carry no site scope in IndexedDB — only collections do — so a legacy collection with siteId == null (deliberately kept visible on every site) drags its entire record set into every other site in the same browser.
evidence: CollectionStorage.ts:44-49 the content store indexes collectionId/status/updatedAt only; CMSContentItem (shared/types/cms.ts:80-90) has no siteId. CollectionManager.ts:62-66 mine() filters `c.siteId === this.projectId || c.siteId == null` — collections only; getContentItems (:343-350) goes straight to Storage.loadContentItems(collectionId) with no scope check.
fix: Stamp siteId on entries at write time (CollectionManager.ts:274) the way collections are stamped at :125, and backfill from the owning collection during refreshFromStorage.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem -> open a second site in the same browser -> (no site scope on entries) -> Content panel -> an unscoped legacy collection and all of its records list under a site that never created them

finding: 'archived' is a documented record status with no writer and no honest handling: nothing sets it, updateContentItem treats it as a plain update, and the sync collapses it to DRAFT — so if it were ever reachable, archiving a live record would quietly unpublish it while emitting content:updated.
evidence: shared/types/cms.ts:86 `status: 'draft' | 'published' | 'archived'`; grep for `"archived"` across src/ finds no CMS writer (the only hits are FormsScreen.tsx:54,119,273, a different feature). CollectionManager.ts:317-323 branches on 'published' only. cmsSync.ts:214 `status: item.status === 'published' ? 'PUBLISHED' : 'DRAFT'`.
fix: Drop 'archived' from CMSContentItem until a surface writes it, or implement it end to end (a distinct server status, an UNPUBLISHED-class event, and exclusion from dynamic-page generation).
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem.status -> archive a record -> content:updated + status mapped to DRAFT -> Publish -> the record silently leaves the live site under an event that says nothing changed

finding: The e-commerce Products offer can create a duplicate Products collection: hasProductsCollection reads the manager's in-memory map, which getAllCollections does NOT initialize, and the block-insert handler can fire before the async hydrate that populates it.
evidence: ProductCollectionService.ts:21-24 `const collections = await this.collectionManager.getAllCollections(); return collections.some(c => c.slug === 'products')`; CollectionManager.ts:178-180 getAllCollections is synchronous over `this.collections` with no ensureInitialized() call (contrast createCollection :112, createContentItem :259 which do await it). useCmsSync.ts:36 `void hydrateCmsFromServer().then(() => cm.refreshFromStorage())` is behind a network round-trip; useComposerInit.ts:747-748 runs the check on ELEMENT_INSERTED. CollectionManager.ts:83-94 documents this exact failure mode ('hasProductsCollection() answered false, which offers to create a SECOND Products collection and mirrors the duplicate back to the server').
fix: Await collectionManager.initialize() (or a hydration-ready promise) inside hasProductsCollection/getProductsCollectionId, or gate the ELEMENT_INSERTED handler on getCmsHydrationStatus() === 'ready'.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection(products) -> insert a product block before hydrate settles -> ELEMENT_INSERTED handler -> Ecommerce setup modal + cmsSync -> a second Products collection is created locally and mirrored to the server

finding: There is no reverse index anywhere: no surface can answer 'which elements or pages use this collection/record/field', so every destructive CMS action (delete collection, delete field, delete record) is taken blind.
evidence: CMSBindingManager stores element->binding only (BaseBindingManager.ts:72) and exposes getBindings(elementId) (:140) — no by-collection lookup exists. ContentViews CollectionView/FieldsView render counts of records, never of usages. The single 'is this bound' read in the product is per-element: SelectionBoxOverlay.tsx:74-75. useContentPanel.ts:176-183 deleteRecord and :202-209 deleteField call straight through with no check.
fix: Add getBindingsByCollection(collectionId)/getBindingsByField(collectionId, slug) to CMSBindingManager, show a usage count on the collection and field rows, and require confirmation naming the affected elements before a delete.
chain: CMS -> CMSCollection/CMSField -> delete -> (no usage query exists) -> Inspector/Canvas -> bindings dangle silently; the user finds out when the published page is blank

finding: One entity, two independently-written record editors that disagree: the Content panel's RecordView and CMSRecordsModal differ on validation surfacing, on delete confirmation and on where a new record's id goes — and the modal's only door is the command palette, which the binding popover then advertises as the way to add records.
evidence: editor/sidebar/tabs/content/ContentViews.tsx RecordView (via useContentPanel.ts:151-174 saveRecord) vs editor/shell/modals/CMSRecordsModal.tsx:138-160 save(); the modal deletes with no confirm (:164-172) while the panel confirms (ContentViews.tsx:619-621 notes CMS records are not on the undo stack). CMS_MANAGE_RECORDS has exactly one emitter — useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:171 — consumed at useEditorEventListeners.ts:90-96. BindingPopover.tsx:294 tells the user 'Add records via the command palette -> "Manage CMS Records"' while the Content drawer sits on the rail. Board halves already filed: W-C-33 (no door), W-O-24 (the copy), W-C-24/W-C-06 (validation).
fix: Make the modal a thin host for the panel's RecordView (one form, one save path, one delete confirm), and point BindingPopover's empty state at the Content drawer.
chain: CMS -> CMSContentItem -> add a record -> two divergent editors -> Content panel / records modal -> behaviour depends on which door the user found, and the popover names the door with no visible entry point

finding: DataBindResolver — five exported functions for parsing data-bind attributes off imported HTML — has zero consumers outside its barrel, alongside six other dead CMS exports; the module carries a second, unwired binding mechanism next to the live one.
evidence: engine/cms/index.ts:13-19 re-exports parseDataBindAttributes, createBindingsFromDataBind, resolveDataBindings, getDataBindFields, hasDataBindAttributes — repo grep finds each only in DataBindResolver.ts and that barrel line. Also unreferenced: CollectionStorage.ts:221 deleteAllContentItems, :255 getContentCount, :115 loadCollectionBySlug; CollectionManager.ts:171 getCollectionBySlug; CMSBindingManager.ts:145 resolveBindingWithContext (the repeater-context resolver, dead with MOD-A-02); ProductCollectionService.ts:98 ensureProductsCollection.
fix: Delete DataBindResolver.ts and the six dead members, or wire getContentCount into the Content panel's record counts (useContentPanel.ts:127-129 currently loads every record just to call .length).
chain: CMS -> data-bind attributes -> import HTML with data-bind markers -> (no caller) -> CMSBindingManager -> the attributes are inert; the only working path is the inspector popover

finding: The inspector registry declares a 'data.repeaterEnabled' toggle that no section renders and no engine field backs — a control advertised in config for the feature MOD-A-01/02 shows is unreachable.
evidence: editor/inspector/config/propertiesRegistry.ts:877 `"data.repeaterEnabled": { uiOnly: true, type: "toggle", responsive: false, states: false, tier: "basic" }`; repo grep for `data.repeater` returns that line only — no renderer, no reader, and CMSCollectionBinding has no `enabled` member (CMSBindingManager.ts:47-60).
fix: Remove the row, or make it the entry point for bindCollection/unbindCollection that MOD-A-01 says is missing.
chain: CMS -> repeater binding -> toggle 'Repeat with collection' -> (registry entry with no renderer) -> Inspector -> the control appears in no panel; the registry describes a feature the UI does not have

finding: DynamicPagesView's page-count is computed from LOCAL records while the pages are generated from SERVER entries, so a pending or failed sync makes the promised count wrong in the direction that hurts — it claims pages that will not be generated.
evidence: ContentViews.tsx:637 `const publishedCount = records.filter(r => r.status === 'published').length` over the panel's IndexedDB-backed rows (useContentPanel.ts:143-149), rendered at :668-673 as 'Generates N pages from published records'. generateDynamicPages reads prisma.cmsEntry `where: {collectionId, status: 'PUBLISHED'}` (cms.service.ts:198-202). cmsSync mirrors best-effort and queues on failure (cmsSync.ts:203-219), and getCmsSyncPendingCount() (:46) is not consulted by this screen.
fix: Show the pending-sync count on this screen (getCmsSyncPendingCount is already exported and already drives a toast in useCmsSync.ts:55), or read the authoritative number from cms.dynamicPages.
chain: CMS -> published entries -> queued sync failure -> (count read locally) -> Dynamic pages screen -> 'Generates 4 pages' over entries the server has never received

finding: CMS_STORE_REFRESHED exists precisely so the server hydration does not re-push rows back to the server, and it works — but it reaches only the Content panel: every other CMS reader (binding popover, records modal, canvas preview) reads on open or on content:* and so shows pre-hydration state if it was already mounted when the hydrate landed.
evidence: CollectionManager.ts:100 emits CMS_STORE_REFRESHED; listeners are ContentTab.tsx:102 only. BindingPopover.tsx:114-118 loads collections on `open`; CMSRecordsModal.tsx:104-110 loads on `isOpen`; useCMSPreview.ts:115-130 listens to content:* only. useCmsSync.ts:36 fires the refresh after a network round-trip, i.e. after the shell has mounted.
fix: Have CMSBindingManager re-apply and useCMSPreview bump its revision on CMS_STORE_REFRESHED — the hydrate can change what every binding resolves to.
chain: CMS -> collections/entries hydrated from the server -> CMS_STORE_REFRESHED -> Canvas preview + inspector popover -> only the Content panel reacts; bound elements keep rendering their fallback until an unrelated content event
